We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1 (forward) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So retrosynthetic step: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid (or activated) and amine.

Step2: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the /C=C/C(=O)N...). So retrosynthetic step: break the C=C double bond and the carboxylic acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> alpha,beta-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So retrosynthesis: from the unsaturated acid fragment (the phenyl ring with /C=C/C(=O)N...), we can disconnect to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). But note the unsaturated acid is attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the fragment is /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (i.e., an amide of aniline). So the unsaturated acid is a cinnamoyl amide (trans). The Doebner modification would give the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) from aldehyde + malonic acid. Then later amide formation attaches the aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

1. Disconnection of sulfonamide: target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring. Sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride + amine. So break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (the phenyl with NH). Actually the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the second phenyl (with the unsaturated amide). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (the methyl phenyl) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (first phenyl with NH2). The first phenyl currently has a methyl and an NH (connected to sulfonyl). So precursor: 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine) maybe.

2. Break amide bond between the unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So give carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid) and aniline (aniline). Actually the amide is between the carbonyl of the unsaturated acid and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursor: trans-cinnamic acid (or its unsaturated acid) and aniline.

3. Break the C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aldehyde (p-? the second phenyl with aldehyde) and malonic acid. The second phenyl is c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to sulfonyl. The unsaturated acid is attached at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the aldehyde precursor would be p-formyl phenyl (4-formyl phenyl) attached to sulfonyl. So we need sulfonyl chloride attached to 4-formyl phenyl.

Thus overall route:

Target -> (1) sulfonamide disconnection -> p-toluidine + 4-(formyl)phenyl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-CHO-SO2Cl). (But the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl bearing the aldehyde). Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring that later will have the unsaturated amide. So precursor: 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). This can be made from 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial maybe). Then step2: amide formation between trans-cinnamic acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Wait the aniline is attached to the unsaturated acid; but after step1 we have sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine. The sulfonyl chloride will react with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide (first step). The unsaturated amide is on the other phenyl (the sulfonyl phenyl). So we need to generate that phenyl with unsaturated amide attached. That is separate: we need to attach the unsaturated amide onto the sulfonyl phenyl via amide formation? Actually the unsaturated amide is attached to the same phenyl (the sulfonyl phenyl) at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl phenyl has a para substituent: the cinnamoyl anilide. So that part is formed via a coupling of the cinnamic acid (or its derivative) with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give the amide, then that amide attached to phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break that amide to give cinnamic acid and aniline. Then break cinnamic acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (Doebner). So we have three steps: (a) sulfonamide formation, (b) amide formation, (c) Doebner modification.

Thus we need templates for each step. We need to find template IDs for sulfonamide formation, amide formation, Doebner modification (which is a Knoevenagel-type condensation with malonic acid). Use search to find templates.

First, get available functional groups list to know correct names.
